the limit laws for the automorphism groups of finite structures are much more subtle and interesting than the zero-one law.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the automorphism group of a random finite structure is not a trivial group with high probability.

, in contrast to the case of rigid structures,  the automorphism group of a nonrigid structure can be ``large'' in many different ways, and that each such way gives rise to a class of nonrigid structures with a limit law.
